problem: Existing LM-based navigation benchmarks emphasize success rate and ignore social compliance, and large LMs (e.g. GPT-4v in VLM-Social-Nav) are too slow and costly for real-time robots. Zero-shot social compliance of GPT-4o and Claude had not been systematically evaluated, and high-quality social navigation data is scarce.
motivation: Robots sharing space with pedestrians must follow social norms, yet frontier LMs are impractical on resource-constrained platforms. A small model trained on little data with parameter-efficient tuning could give fast, deployable, socially aware decisions.
key_idea: Train a small VLM (SigLIP + Phi-2 2.7B) in two stages, SFT that updates only the projector on multi-turn dialogues, then DPO that updates only LoRA on chosen/rejected action pairs, to get socially compliant navigation decisions efficiently from small data.
insight: With only 265 training samples, freezing the backbone and training only the projector in SFT works best (SFT projector-only beat projector+LoRA and +vision tower on most metrics, and had higher FPS). Adding DPO with LoRA on top raises action accuracy from 0.433 to 0.550 and improves all semantic metrics. Backbone choice matters: SigLIP+Phi-2 was best among the VT/SLM combinations tested, and TinyLlama-1.1B was clearly worse.
method: Base architecture: LLaVA-style VLM with a vision tower (SigLIP best; CLIP and DINOv2 tested), a two-layer MLP projector and a small LM (Phi-2 2.7B; TinyLlama-1.1B and StableLM-2-Zephyr-1.6B tested).

Stage I SFT: only the projector is trained, using multi-turn dialogue (perception, prediction, action) per image, with next-token NLL loss on assistant responses only; 20 epochs, lr 5e-5, warmup 0.03, FlashAttention-2.
Stage II DPO: only the LoRA adapter is trained, on single-turn pairs; beta=0.1, 5 epochs.
DPO data construction: the chosen response is the human-annotated answer, and the rejected response is made by editing facts (e.g. the action or speed) in the chosen one.
Dataset: 325 egocentric samples derived from SNEI (SCAND + MuSoHu), each with a five-turn conversation; 265 for training and 60 for testing.
Evaluation: BERTScore P/R/F1, SBERT cosine, Sentence Mover's Similarity, FPS and action accuracy (exact match with the GT action).

setting.backbone: SigLIP + Phi-2-2.7B (projector SFT, then LoRA DPO)
setting.training_data: 265 multi-turn dialogue image samples from SNEI (SCAND/MuSoHu), plus a DPO set of chosen/rejected pairs derived from them
setting.action_space: high-level text actions (e.g. stop, continue straight at a moderate speed, turn left at a slow speed)

numbers.eval_set_note: 60 randomly held-out samples of the 325-sample multi-dialog set derived from SNEI
numbers.extra: trained on only 265 samples; own train/test split
numbers.evidence: Table 1, E-SocialNav (Ours) SFT(projector) + DPO(lora), best in bold

numbers_note: Custom offline text-level metrics, not a standard navigation benchmark; no SR/SPL. Baselines in Table 1: GPT-4o AA 0.450, Claude AA 0.417, Social-LLaVA (Vicuna-7B) AA 0.483.
results: E-SocialNav (2.7B) reaches AA 0.550 and BERTScore-F1 0.688, beating the strongest baseline Social-LLaVA (7B, fine-tuned; AA 0.483, F1 0.641) and zero-shot GPT-4o (AA 0.450). It is also faster (2.354 FPS vs 1.113 for Social-LLaVA).
limitations: Tiny test set (60 samples) with a single dataset and no closed-loop or real-robot evaluation.
Human annotations are biased toward conservative actions (e.g. GT 'turn left slowly' vs predicted 'stop'), and social norms are hard to standardize.
Efficiency claims (energy, latency) are supported only by FPS, not by on-device measurements.
